title: Mid-Autumn Festival
summary: A family gathered beneath the moon: harvest, gratitude and reunion.

title: Halloween
summary: Play, hospitality, unease and remembrance at the threshold of winter.

title: Bonfire Night
summary: The history beneath an autumn evening of bonfires and fireworks.

title: Diwali
summary: Lamps, homecoming and the many meanings of a shared season.

title: Remembrance Sunday
summary: A national pause to honour service and sacrifice, on the Sunday set aside for remembrance.

title: Indigenous Veterans Day
summary: Canada’s day of honour for First Nations, Inuit and Métis veterans, and for what they were denied.

title: Intersex Day of Solidarity
summary: A day of remembrance and solidarity, marked on the birthday of Herculine Barbin.

title: Synaxis of the Archangel Michael
summary: An Orthodox feast honouring the archangels and the other heavenly powers.

title: Victory Day (Azerbaijan)
summary: Azerbaijan’s national holiday marking the recapture of Shusha on 8 November 2020.

title: World Radiography Day
summary: The anniversary of the X-ray, and a thank-you to the people who use it to see inside the body.

title: World Town Planning Day
summary: A day for the quiet craft of making places that people can live in well.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: The anniversary of 9 November 1989, when East Germany’s border opened after 28 years and the Cold War’s sharpest symbol began to fall.

title: Kristallnacht
summary: The anniversary of the November 1938 pogrom across Nazi Germany, a turning point on the road to the Holocaust.

title: Independence Day (Cambodia)
summary: Cambodia’s national holiday for its 1953 independence from France.

title: Amavasya (new moon day, Diwali week)
summary: The new moon day that runs until midday in New Delhi, the gap day between Diwali and Govardhan Puja this year.

title: Govardhan Puja (Annakut)
summary: The fourth day of Diwali, when Hindus offer a “mountain of food” to Krishna for lifting Govardhan Hill.

title: Atatürk Memorial Day (Turkey)
summary: Turkey falls silent at 09:05 to remember Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, who died at that minute on 10 November 1938.

title: World Science Day for Peace and Development
summary: UNESCO’s yearly day for science in society; the 2026 theme is “Common ground through science diplomacy”.

title: Bestu Varas (Gujarati New Year)
summary: The Gujarati New Year, opening Vikram Samvat 2083 the day after Diwali’s gap day.

title: US Marine Corps Birthday
summary: The 251st birthday of the US Marine Corps, founded by the Continental Congress on 10 November 1775.

title: Sesame Street’s birthday
summary: Sesame Street first aired on 10 November 1969; it turns 57 today.

title: Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald
summary: The 51st anniversary of the Lake Superior shipwreck that took 29 lives and inspired Gordon Lightfoot’s ballad.

title: Armistice Day (Remembrance Day)
summary: At 11am the UK and Commonwealth keep two minutes’ silence, 108 years after the guns of the First World War fell quiet.

title: Veterans Day (United States)
summary: America’s federal holiday honouring everyone who has served in its armed forces, born from Armistice Day.

title: Polish National Independence Day
summary: Poland celebrates regaining its independence on 11 November 1918, after 123 years wiped off the map.

title: Bhai Dooj
summary: The last day of Diwali, when sisters mark a tilak on their brothers’ foreheads and pray for their long life.

title: St Martin’s Day (Martinmas)
summary: The feast of St Martin of Tours: lantern processions, roast goose and, once, the end of the farming year.

title: Carnival season opens at 11:11 (Germany)
summary: At 11:11 on 11.11, Cologne, Düsseldorf and Mainz kick off the “fifth season” of carnival.

title: Singles’ Day (China)
summary: China’s tongue-in-cheek day for the unattached, born at Nanjing University in 1993, now the world’s biggest shopping festival.

title: Angola Independence Day
summary: Angola marks 51 years since Agostinho Neto proclaimed independence from Portugal on 11 November 1975.

title: World Pneumonia Day
summary: A global day of action against pneumonia, the world’s biggest infectious killer of children and a major threat to older adults, held every 12 November since 2009.

title: Dr Sun Yat-sen’s Birthday (Taiwan)
summary: Taiwan remembers the doctor-turned-revolutionary born on 12 November 1866, ‘Father of the Nation’ of the Republic of China; the date is also Chinese Cultural Renaissance Day and Doctors’ Day.

title: Anniversary of the World Wide Web proposal (1990)
summary: On 12 November 1990 Tim Berners-Lee and Robert Cailliau put forward the formal proposal at CERN that gave the World Wide Web its name.

title: Scott’s polar party found (1912)
summary: On 12 November 1912 a search party found the snow-covered tent holding the bodies of Captain Scott, Edward Wilson and Henry Bowers on the Antarctic ice.

title: Voyager 1 at Saturn (1980)
summary: On 12 November 1980 Voyager 1 swept past Titan and made its closest approach to Saturn, revealing braided rings, new moons and Titan’s orange haze.

title: Philae lands on a comet (2014)
summary: On 12 November 2014 the European Space Agency’s Philae lander made the first ever touchdown on a comet, then bounced across its surface before coming to rest in the shadows.

title: Public Service Broadcasting Day (India)
summary: India remembers Mahatma Gandhi’s only visit to the All India Radio studios, on 12 November 1947, when he spoke to Partition refugees at Kurukshetra.

title: BBC Children in Need Appeal Night
summary: The BBC’s own children’s charity holds its 47th appeal night, a three-hour live telethon from Salford with Pudsey Bear, a nationwide children’s choir and landmarks lit up yellow.

title: World Kindness Day
summary: Held every 13 November since 1998, when the first World Kindness Movement conference opened in Tokyo, a day for small good deeds that cross borders, faiths and cultures.

title: Martyrdom of Fatimah al-Zahra (Iran)
summary: Iran’s national day of mourning for Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, on 3 Jumada al-Thani, the high point of the Shia Fatimiyya season; the date follows the lunar calendar and can shift by a day.

title: Wangala, the Hundred Drums Festival
summary: The Garo people’s post-harvest thanksgiving to the sun god Misi Saljong, a public holiday in Meghalaya, India, today, with this year’s big celebration planned around 1,000 drums.

title: Friday the 13th
summary: The third and last Friday the 13th of 2026, a rare three-in-a-year run, and a look at where the superstition really comes from.

title: Robert Louis Stevenson born (1850)
summary: The author of Treasure Island, Kidnapped and Jekyll and Hyde was born in Edinburgh on 13 November 1850, 176 years ago today.

title: World Diabetes Day
summary: Held every 14 November on the birthday of Frederick Banting, co-discoverer of insulin, the world's largest diabetes awareness campaign. The 2026 theme is “Early action on diabetes”.

title: Moby-Dick published in America (1851)
summary: On 14 November 1851 Harper & Brothers published Herman Melville's Moby-Dick in New York, 175 years ago today. It sold poorly, then became one of the great novels in English.

title: Children’s Day (Bal Diwas), India
summary: India celebrates its children every 14 November, the birthday of its first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, born in 1889 and fondly known as Chacha Nehru.

title: Chhath Puja: Kharna
summary: Day two of the four-day Hindu festival of Chhath, devoted to the Sun god and Chhathi Maiya. After a day's fast, devotees eat a sweet kheer at dusk and then begin a 36-hour fast without water.

title: The King’s birthday
summary: King Charles III was born at Buckingham Palace on 14 November 1948 and turns 78 today, an official flag-flying day on UK government buildings.

title: The Coventry Blitz (1940)
summary: On the night of 14 to 15 November 1940, German bombers devastated Coventry in an 11-hour raid that destroyed its medieval cathedral and gave birth to a lasting ministry of reconciliation.

title: Claude Monet born (1840)
summary: The father of Impressionism was born in Paris on 14 November 1840, 186 years ago today, in the year that also marks the centenary of his death.
